title: The Library After Dark

before.title: The Library After Dark
before.text: Workers in one town finish late. The public library closes before many of them can visit. At a town meeting, a nurse asks for one late evening each week. The library cannot pay for more hours every day. It moves some morning hours to Thursday night. After a short test, more workers and students use the library.

after.title: The Library After Dark
after.text:
This library and its town are imagined. Many workers finished after the library closed. At a meeting, a nurse asked whether it could open late one evening a week.

The staff checked their hours and tried moving some time from Thursday morning to Thursday night. They put the new hours on the door.

After four weeks, they counted evening visits and asked people when they came. The town used the results to decide whether to keep the new hours.

title: The Lion and the Small Helper

before.title: The Lion and the Small Helper
before.text: A lion finds a mouse and holds it under one paw. The mouse asks to go free and promises to help one day. The lion laughs but lets it go. Later, the lion is caught in a rope net. The mouse hears his call. It cuts the rope with its small teeth until the lion can get free. A small friend can give great help.

title: The Shared Street Light

before.title: The Shared Street Light
before.text: Two villages meet at a dark road. Each village says the other should pay for a street light. A nurse explains that people from both places use the road at night. The leaders agree to share the cost. One village buys the lamp, and the other pays for power and repairs.

after.title: The Shared Street Light
after.text:
This story takes place in two imagined villages. People from both places used a dark road at night. Each village thought the other should pay for a light.

At a meeting, a nurse described her trip home along the road. The leaders agreed to share the work. One village paid for the lamp. The other paid the power bill and arranged repairs.

They wrote down who would check the light if it stopped working. The two villages had made a plan for the road they both used.

title: Waves on a Stick Chart

before.title: Shells and Waves on a Stick Chart
before.text: People of the Marshall Islands made special charts from sticks and shells. The sticks showed how ocean waves moved around islands. Small shells could show the islands. People learned by watching the sea and traveling with skilled teachers. A chart was not always carried on a trip. Much of the map lived in their memory.

after.title: Waves on a Stick Chart
after.text:
Navigators in the Marshall Islands made charts from sticks and shells. Curved sticks could show the ways ocean swells changed around islands. Small shells could mark islands or atolls.

The charts helped learners understand wave patterns. They were usually used for teaching on land, rather than carried on a voyage like a modern map.

At sea, a skilled navigator also watched and felt the movement of the water. Learning the chart was one part of learning to read the sea.

reason: The Smithsonian identifies the Marshallese stick charts as training and instruction tools that were not generally carried to sea. State that role directly and clarify shells as island markers.

title: Colors in a Drop of Rain

before.title: Colors in a Drop of Rain
before.text: Light from the Sun may look white, but it holds many colors. When light enters a drop of water, it changes direction. The light also turns back inside the drop and changes direction again as it leaves. The colors do not all change direction in the same way. Many drops together can make a rainbow across the sky.

title: Black Beauty Finds a Last Home

before.title: Black Beauty Finds a Gentle Home
before.text: Black Beauty tells the story of his life as a horse. Some owners are kind, but others use painful equipment or work him too hard. He meets horses who have also suffered. After illness and difficult years, Beauty is sold to people who treat him gently. He ends his life in a safe green field.

after.title: Black Beauty Finds a Last Home
after.text:
Black Beauty tells the story of his life as a horse. Some people treat him kindly. Others make him work too hard or use equipment that hurts him.

After many difficult years, he comes to a quiet home. A man named Joe Green knows him from long ago. The people who care for Beauty promise that he will not be sold again.

Beauty can rest in the field and feel safe. His story ends there, with his new home and the people who remember him.
